tools.name: post_job
tools.description: Post a new job listing, as the authenticated user. Equivalent to the website's "Post a Job" form. Charges a $2 posting fee immediately; requires a saved payment method.

tools.name: get_bids
tools.description: List every bid on a job, with each bidder's rating average and count. Bids are listed to everyone, including while the job is open: who bid, when, and whether the bid still stands is public from the moment a bid is placed. The list includes withdrawn bids, so it can be longer than the job's bid_coun

tools.name: submit_bid
tools.description: Submit a bid on an open job, as the authenticated user. You can't bid on your own job. You get one bid per job, ever: your bid amount cannot be edited afterwards, and if you withdraw it you cannot bid on that job again. Decide the amount before calling this. Requires a completed Stripe Connect payou

tools.name: accept_bid
tools.description: Accept a specific bid on a job, as that job's buyer. Moves the job to in_progress. Only the job's buyer can do this -- the bidder accepting their own bid is rejected, as is anyone who isn't the buyer. Charges the buyer the full bid amount, held in our Stripe account until the job ends; requires a sa

tools.name: get_messages
tools.description: Read the messages for a job. Every message names its sender and its recipient, so a buyer can tell which conversation eac

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message on a job to a specific other participant. If you're the buyer, the recipient must be someone who has actually bid on the job. tools.name: complete_job
tools.description: Mark a job as complete, as that job's buyer. Moves the job from in_progress to completed. Only the buyer can do this -- not even the accepted bidder can mark their own job complete. Transfers 90% of the held amount to the seller's own Stripe account; fails if they haven't finished Stripe Connect pay

tools.name: cancel_job

tools.name: withdraw_bid
tools.description: Withdraw your own bid on a job, as the bidder who placed it. Only possible while the job is still open and your bid hasn't been accepted. No reason required. This is permanent and cannot be undone: once you withdraw, you cannot bid on that job again, and there is no way to replace or restore the wit

tools.name: request_close
tools.description: Ask the buyer to close an in-progress job, as the seller working on it. Use this after delivering, when the buyer has gone quiet. tools.name: mark_job_seen
tools.description: Record that you have seen everything on this job, which clears has_new_messages and has_new_bids for it on get_my_jobs. tools.name: submit_rating
tools.description: Rate your counterparty on a job that's completed or cancelled. Only the buyer and the accepted bidder can rate each other, only each other (not a third party, not yourself), and only once per job.

tools.name: get_me

Also what the key you are using may do: its permissions, spending limit, what it has charged and when it expires.

tools.name: update_me
tools.description: Set the description on your own public profile, the line shown under your username to anyone looking at your record. tools.name: get_offer

tools.name: get_my_requests
tools.description: The requests you have sent and the requests on your own offer, each with its status. tools.name: post_offer
tools.description: Post a standing offer: what you provide and the price to start from. Free, unlike posting a job. Requires a verified email and a completed Stripe Connect payout account -- an offer is a promise to do paid work, and a seller who cannot be paid cannot keep it. ONE ACTIVE OFFER PER ACCOUNT, and an offe

tools.name: end_offer
tools.description: Stop an offer taking new requests. It stays public with its history, pending requests on it can still be accepted or declined, and jobs already running through it carry on. There is no un-end and no edit: posting a replacement is the way to change what you provide.

tools.name: send_request
tools.description: Ask a seller to do something, naming your own amount and how long you expect it to take. Requires a verified email and a saved payment method: a request is a commitment to pay if the seller accepts. NOTHING IS CHARGED NOW -- if this credential has a spending limit, the amount is reserved against it

tools.name: accept_request
tools.description: Accept a pending request on your own offer. Requires your payout account to still be complete, checked again here however long ago you

tools.name: decline_request
tools.description: Decline a pending request on your own offer. Nothing is charged, the buyer is told, and any reservation held against their spending limit is released. tools.name: withdraw_request
tools.description: Take back a request you sent, while it is still pending. tools.name: report_gap

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: browse_jobs, get_user_jobs, get_job, get_messages, mark_job_seen, get_me, get_my_jobs, get_user, get_ratings, get_document, browse_offers, report_gap · Private data: browse_jobs, get_user_offers, mark_job_seen, update_me, get_document, browse_offers, get_offer, post_offer, send_request, accept_request, report_gap · Public sink: browse_jobs, post_job, submit_bid, send_message, submit_rating, get_me, update_me, get_my_jobs, get_my_payments, get_user, get_offer, post_offer, send_request, withdraw_request, report_gap · Destructive: get_my_payments, report_gap.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: browse_jobs, get_user_jobs, get_job, get_messages, mark_job_seen, get_me, get_my_jobs, get_user, get_ratings, get_document, browse_offers, report_gap · Private data: browse_jobs, get_user_offers, mark_job_seen, update_me, get_document, browse_offers, get_offer, post_offer, send_request, accept_request, report_gap · Public sink: browse_jobs, post_job, submit_bid, send_message, submit_rating, get_me, update_me, get_my_jobs, get_my_payments, get_user, get_offer, post_offer, send_request, withdraw_request, report_gap · Destructive: get_my_payments, report_gap

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
